naming: The loader deserializes with YamlDotNet's CamelCaseNamingConvention and refuses any key it does not know.

keys.description: Optional grouping label (the source system) the platform files the flow's pipeline and runs under. A blank value counts as none.
Optional text describing what the inventories are for.

The document kind: `inventory`, every id and version OSDU kinds hold in a partition, kept in the module database and compared with every ledger of the partition: records no ledger knows (orphans), records a ledger expects that OSDU does not serve (missing), ids an unfinished delivery left (undoing), and records a ledger forgot. A build, a reconcile and a plan only read OSDU; a flow that declares `removal` also lets an operator remove the orphan, stale or forgotten ids it found, and any inventory flow lets an operator remove its gone ids from the inventory alone.

The inventories, at least one and at most 100, names unique ignoring case. Each holds every id one kind holds in the partition, with its version, who created and last changed it and when, when it was first listed and when it went, and what the ledgers hold of it.
One inventory: the kind it reads (`kind`), narrowed by a search `query`, and whether it keeps every version of each record (`versions`).
Optional text describing what the inventory holds.

The kind read, `authority:source:entityType:version`, each segment a value, `*`, or a value with `*` inside it (`1.*.*`), matched ignoring case as the search service matches a kind. An inventory that names its entity type and leaves the other three segments and the query open covers its type whole: a ledger's delivered record, or live minted id, of the type that the read did not list is then read from storage and reported `missing` or `unlisted`. An inventory narrowed further reports only the ids it listed before and no longer lists.
The inventory's name: a letter or digit followed by letters, digits, '.', '_' and '-', at most 100 characters. A run's payload (`inventories`), the report and the CLI name it by it.
A Lucene query narrowing the records a search read lists; `{name}` tokens of `parameters` and `{partition}` are filled in. A storage read takes none, and the flow is refused when one is written.

`latest` (the default) keeps each record's latest version, which every read returns. `all` also keeps every version storage keeps of each record, read (GET /records/versions/{id}) for a record that is new or whose latest version moved since its versions were read, so a rebuild sends requests only for what moved.

How many ids a ledger expects that one build reads from storage to tell `missing` (storage does not hold it) from `unlisted` (storage holds it, and the read did not list it), between 0 (none: they are reported `gone`) and 1,000,000. Never-asked ids first, then the longest ago asked; successive builds take turns through all of them. An id a build did not ask keeps what storage last answered; one never asked is `gone` until a build asks. A build that reaches the bound says so.
The inventory flow's name: its pipeline identity, and the name its inventories are kept under. A flow that reads partitions keeps its inventories per partition.

The identities this estate's records are written as (OSDU's `createUser`: a user's e-mail, an application's client id), at most 50, unique ignoring case. An id no ledger of the partition knows is an `orphan` when one of them created it, and `foreign` when another identity did. Left out, a build infers them: every identity that created at least 1% of the ids of the inventory a ledger claims, and says so.
One identity, as OSDU writes it as a record's `createUser`, at most 256 characters, no whitespace.
What one run works on at once: `recordsAtOnce`, how many version lists a build reads at once. An inventory flow fans nothing out across the fleet.
How many version lists of an inventory keeping every version a build reads at once. At least 1.
Renamed: it is written as `parallelism.recordsAtOnce`, as on a delivery flow. A document that still declares it is refused when it loads, naming the key it is now.
Optional: the flow's parameters, by name. `{name}` tokens are usable in an inventory's `query`; `{partition}` is always the partition the run reads, and may not be declared.
One parameter; `<name>` is the name its `{name}` tokens use. A run supplying a value for a name the flow does not declare is refused.

The values the parameter may take, in the order a run form lists them: a run given any other value is refused (`parameter 'name' is given 'x', which is not one of its choices: a, b.`), and the run form offers them as a list to pick from. At least one and at most 500, each listed once and written as a run gives it; a `default` is one of them. Leave it out for a parameter that takes any value.
One value the parameter may take.
The value used when a run supplies none; one of the parameter's `choices` when it lists them.
Text describing what the parameter is for.
When true, a run that supplies no value, for a parameter without a default, fails with "parameter 'name' is required". A scheduled fire supplies only the schedule's `values`, so give it one there.

The OSDU data partitions the flow keeps inventories of, hard-coded: each by its `data-partition-id` written literally, never a reference, at least one, unique ignoring case. Leave it out to read the partition `source.headers` names, or every partition registered with the catalog when the headers name none. A run reads one partition.
One partition the flow keeps inventories of, by its `data-partition-id`.
The HTTP settings: timeout, retry, rate limit, TLS, URL allowlist and response size. What runs at once is `parallelism`.

Not a setting here any more: a delivery flow writes it as `parallelism.recordsPerBatch`, and an inventory flow has no use for it. A document that still declares it is refused when it loads; remove it.
Not a setting any more: a worker claims the records due for a retry `parallelism.recordsAtOnce` at a time, at least 50. A document that still declares it is refused when it loads; remove it.

Not a setting here any more: it is written as `parallelism.recordsAtOnce`, since what runs at once, and across the fleet, is the flow's parallelism, and reliability keeps what makes a request hold. A document that still declares it here is refused when it loads, naming where it goes.
Not a setting here any more: a delivery flow writes it as `parallelism.nodes`, and an inventory flow has no use for it. A document that still declares it is refused when it loads; remove it.
Not a setting here any more: a delivery flow writes it as `parallelism.minRowsPerNode`, and an inventory flow has no use for it. A document that still declares it is refused when it loads; remove it.
A delivery flow's setting: how long a worker's lease on a record lasts. The loader accepts it as on a delivery flow; an inventory flow does not use it.
A delivery flow's setting: the target's declared request body ceiling (0 = not declared). The loader accepts it as on a delivery flow; an inventory flow does not use it.
The largest response body read, in bytes. A larger response fails the request with a message naming this setting.

Not a setting here any more: a delivery flow writes it as `parallelism.interfacesAtOnce`, and an inventory flow has no use for it. A document that still declares it is refused when it loads; remove it.
The most requests per second the flow sends to the platform; 0 means unlimited. Token requests are not limited.
Not a setting here any more: a delivery flow writes it as `parallelism.renderThreads`, and an inventory flow has no use for it. A document that still declares it is refused when it loads; remove it.
How one request is repeated inline. Only requests that are safe to repeat are repeated, on 408, 425, 429, 503 and 504 and on a transport failure; 500 and 502 are not replayed.
The most attempts one request gets, the first included.
The wait between attempts: `exponential` doubles `baseDelayMs` per attempt, `fixed` waits `baseDelayMs` each time; both are capped at `maxDelayMs`.
The first wait between attempts, in milliseconds.

Whether a `Retry-After` the service sends is honoured. A requested wait within `maxDelayMs` becomes the floor of the backoff; a longer one is never shortened, so the request stops instead of waiting it out.
The longest wait between attempts, in milliseconds.
A delivery flow's setting: the first wait between a record's attempts across worker passes, in minutes. The loader accepts it as on a delivery flow; an inventory flow does not use it.
A delivery flow's setting: the longest wait between a record's attempts across worker passes, in minutes. The loader accepts it as on a delivery flow; an inventory flow does not use it.
A delivery flow's setting: statuses that hold a record instead of retrying it. The loader accepts it as on a delivery flow; an inventory flow does not use it.
One HTTP status code.
How long one HTTP request may take, in seconds.

The hosts requests may reach (an SSRF guard), checked on every request and every redirect hop. Empty allows any host the deployment's network policy reaches; token requests are not checked against it.
A host name, or `*.suffix` to match the bare domain and any subdomain of it. Compared ignoring case.
Whether the platform's TLS certificate is verified. `false` also needs `SQLFLOW_DELIVERY_ALLOW_INSECURE_TLS=true` on the node, or the run is refused.

What an operator may remove from OSDU of what the inventories found: the ids of the findings `findings` names, through the flow's own `source` and credentials, soft deleted (POST /records/delete, 500 ids a request, reversible), or purged (DELETE /records/{id}, every version destroyed) when `purge` allows it. Left out, the flow only reads OSDU and nothing it found can be removed through it. A removal is a run of the flow (operation `remove`) an operator asks for from the inventory's page: it confirms the partition and the number of ids shown, checks every id again just before it goes (its finding, what the ledgers hold of it now, its version, an orphan's creator), and keeps what it did to each id. The source's credentials must be an owner of the records (`users.datalake.editors`, and in each record's owners ACL).

The findings whose ids may be removed, at least one, each once: `orphan` (no ledger knows it, and an owner created it), `stale` (a ledger marks its record removed, or an undo its id, and OSDU still serves it) or `forgotten` (its record was purged from its ledger). A stale record's ledger records the removal on the record. Every other finding is acted on through its ledger.
One finding whose ids an operator may remove.

When true, a removal may purge (DELETE /records/{id}: the record and every version destroyed for good, one request per id) rather than soft delete. Left false, removals only soft delete, which OSDU can revert.
The OSDU platform the inventories are read from, and how. A build only reads: nothing is ever written to OSDU.

How requests to the OSDU platform authenticate, written as `target.auth` is on a delivery flow. Secrets are references only: ${env:NAME} or ${keyvault:vault/secret}. Left out, requests carry no credentials (type `none`).
keys.appliesWhen: Optional; written as `target.auth` on a delivery flow.

keys.description: The header an `apiKeyHeader` auth sends the key in.
keys.appliesWhen: source.auth.type is apiKeyHeader, which needs it.

keys.description: The secondary secret, as a reference (${env:NAME} or ${keyvault:vault/secret}): the username for `basic`, the client id for `oauth2ClientCredentials` (sent as `client_id` unless the token body names one).

The primary secret, as a reference (${env:NAME} or ${keyvault:vault/secret}), never a literal: the token for `bearer`, the key for `apiKeyHeader`, the password for `basic`, the client secret for `oauth2ClientCredentials` (sent as `client_secret` unless the token body names one). A literal is refused when the flow is read.
keys.appliesWhen: Needed by bearer, apiKeyHeader and basic; used by oauth2ClientCredentials.

keys.description: The OAuth2 token endpoint: where a token is requested and how it is read from the answer. One token serves the run and is requested again shortly before it expires.
keys.appliesWhen: source.auth.type is oauth2ClientCredentials, which needs it.

keys.description: The text put before the access token in the `Authorization` header.
When true, the client id and secret are sent as an HTTP Basic `Authorization` header on the token request instead of in its form body.

Extra form fields of the token request, by name. `grant_type` is `client_credentials` unless set here, and `client_id` and `client_secret` come from `secondarySecretRef` and `secretRef` unless set here. A field named as a secret (`client_secret`, `password`, `refresh_token`, `client_assertion`, ...) holds a reference only; a literal there is refused when the flow is read. `client_id`, `scope` and `audience` may be literals.

One form field of the token request; `<name>` is the field name (such as `scope`). The value may be a reference (${env:NAME} or ${keyvault:vault/secret}), resolved before the request is sent. A field named as a secret must be a reference.

An OIDC discovery document whose `token_endpoint` is the token URL. When set it is used instead of `url`; it may be a reference. Written literally, its user info and query may carry no credential: one that does is refused when the flow is read.
keys.appliesWhen: source.auth.type is oauth2ClientCredentials; give this or url.

keys.description: The path of the access token in the token endpoint's JSON answer.
The token endpoint URL, usually a reference such as `${env:OSDU_TOKEN_URL}`. Written literally, its user info and query may carry no credential: one that does is refused when the flow is read.
keys.appliesWhen: source.auth.type is oauth2ClientCredentials; give this or discoveryUrl.

keys.description: The auth scheme: `none`, `bearer` (a token as a reference), `apiKeyHeader` (a key in a named header), `basic` (username and password) or `oauth2ClientCredentials` (a token requested from `token`). Read ignoring case.
The text put before the secret in the header value of a `bearer` or `apiKeyHeader` auth. An OAuth2 token takes `token.applyPrefix` instead.
Storage's soft delete of a list of records, which a removal sends 500 ids at a time (it falls back one id at a time where the deployment refuses the list).
Storage's soft delete of one record, naming it as `{id}`: what a removal falls back to for an id the bulk soft delete did not take.
The base URL of the OSDU platform, usually a reference such as `${env:OSDU_URL}`. Written literally, its user info and query may carry no credential: one that does is refused when the flow is read.
Headers sent with every request. A flow that names its partitions, or reads every registered one, may not name `data-partition-id` here: each run sets it to the partition it reads.

One header; `<name>` is the header name (`data-partition-id: dev`). A value may be a reference (${env:NAME} or ${keyvault:vault/secret}). A header that carries a credential (`Authorization`, an API or subscription key, a token, any `x-api-*` header) holds a reference, after its scheme when it has one (`Bearer ${env:NAME}`); a literal is refused when the flow is read.

Storage's read of up to 1,000 records' system properties by id (openapi storage v2, POST /query/records/headers). Where a deployment does not serve it (404 or 405), records are read through `recordQueryPath`, a hundred at a time.

How a read of every record a search matches pages through them. `cursor` (the default) pages the search service's cursor (POST /query_with_cursor), a context the service holds between pages and moves on with each, so a read that loses a page reads the search again from its first page. `createTime` pages the plain search (POST /query) in the order of each record's createTime and then its id, each page asked from the last record handed out: the service holds nothing between pages, a page that fails is asked again from where the read stopped, and a read that comes back short reads again only the batch of about 10,000 records it is short in. Either way a search is read whole or the read fails.
Storage's purge of one record and every version of it, naming it as `{id}`: what a removal that purges sends, one id at a time.
The search service's offset search, which a plan counts an inventory's records through (openapi search v2, POST /query).

How the inventories read OSDU. `search` (the default) pages the search index with a viewer's entitlements; the index lags writes and leaves out a record it failed to index, so a record written seconds before, or never indexed, is not listed, and a ledger's record of it is reported `unlisted`. `storage` lists every active record of each kind from storage itself (GET /query/records?kind=, which needs the storage service's admin role) and reads their system properties a thousand at a time: the complete answer, unindexed records included. A kind with wildcards is expanded through the schema service for a storage read.
Storage's listing of a kind's record ids (GET) and its read of records by id (POST), openapi storage v2 /query/records.
The schema service, which expands a kind with wildcards into the kinds a storage read lists one at a time.
The search service's cursor search, which a search read pages an inventory through, a thousand ids a page, whole or failing (openapi search v2, POST /query_with_cursor).
Storage's list of a record's versions (openapi storage v2, GET /records/versions/{id}), read for an inventory with `versions: all`.
